questions.question: When making tight maneuvers, what should a driver do?

options.text: Open the door for a better look.
Use their mirrors.
Flash their headlights.
Open their cargo door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use their mirrors.
questions.explanation: You should check your mirrors regularly while driving. It is especially important to check them when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight maneuvers.

questions.question: If your wheels spin when accelerating on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use the brakes.
Take your foot off the accelerator.
Continue to accelerate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the accelerator.
questions.explanation: If your drive wheels start to spin while accelerating on a slippery surface, release the accelerator.

questions.question: What is listed in Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table?

options.text: The names of the materials.
Where the materials originated.
Special provisions for the materials.
The costs of the materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: The names of the materials.
questions.explanation: Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table shows the proper shipping names and descriptions of regulated materials.

questions.question: If hazardous materials are leaking from your cargo and you have no phone, what should you do?

options.text: Drive to a phone to alert emergency personnel.
Drive to a designated hazardous materials clean-up facility.
Send someone else for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Send someone else for help.
questions.explanation: If hazardous materials leak, do not drive your vehicle any more than necessary. Driving spreads contamination over a larger area. Instead, park your vehicle safely, stay with it, and contact emergency personnel. If you cannot make the call yourself, send someone else to get help.

questions.question: What should you know about restrictions on transporting explosives or hazardous waste?

options.text: They are usually not a concern.
They are waived on weekends.
You should research them before choosing your route.
They only apply if transporting more than 1,000 pounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should research them before choosing your route.
questions.explanation: Before transporting hazardous materials, research any restrictions that apply to your planned routes.

questions.question: When transporting explosives, what is required?

options.text: You must have a written route plan.
You should take the shortest possible route.
You can always use tunnels.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must have a written route plan.
questions.explanation: When transporting certain types of explosives, you must follow a written route plan. Avoid heavily populated areas, crowds, tunnels, narrow streets, and alleys. Research any restrictions that apply to your planned routes.

questions.question: If you are unsure if your vehicle can safely pass under a bridge, what should you do?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Swerve as you pass under the bridge.
Slow down.
Drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit safely under an overhead object, slow down and find another route if possible.

questions.question: Why should tank drivers reduce speed on curves?

options.text: They can take curves at the posted speed limit.
Tanks have a high center of gravity and can easily roll over.
They should drive on the shoulder whenever possible.
They should slam on their brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tanks have a high center of gravity and can easily roll over.
questions.explanation: Tanks are at high risk of rolling over because of their high center of gravity. Take curves at speeds well below the posted speed limit.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down while transporting explosives, how should you warn other drivers?

options.text: With flares.
With reflective triangles.
By standing on the roadway and waving your arms.

questions.correctAnswerText: With reflective triangles.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down while transporting explosives, use reflective triangles or red electric lights to warn other drivers. Never use flares or other burning signals with explosives.

questions.question: What should you check on the hoses of a vehicle with power steering?

options.text: For leaks.
For the proper amount of brake fluid.
To ensure that they are connected to the battery.

questions.correctAnswerText: For leaks.
questions.explanation: When checking a vehicle with power steering, inspect the hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Look especially for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: What information does a shipping paper provide?

options.text: What materials are being transported
How the materials will be transported
Who should receive the materials

questions.correctAnswerText: What materials are being transported
questions.explanation: Shipping papers must include a description of the hazardous materials being transported.

questions.question: If a vehicle has an inspection report from the previous driver, what should you do?

options.text: Skip your own inspection and trust the previous driver's report.
Take the vehicle to a mechanic.
Read and review the report.
Talk to the previous driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read and review the report.
questions.explanation: Before starting your inspection, read the report left by the previous driver.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.
Roll down your window to listen for a train.
Depend only on traffic signals.
Never try to beat an approaching train across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never try to beat an approaching train across the tracks.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you approach a railroad crossing. You may not hear a train, and signals may not warn you. Never try to race a train across the tracks.

questions.question: How should you load cargo to reduce the risk of a rollover?

options.text: Load it as far forward as possible.
Load it as far back as possible.
Load it as low as possible.
Stack it as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Load it as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep cargo as close to the ground as possible to lower rollover risk. Also take curves and corners slowly.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a sign of bad brakes?

options.text: Cracked drums
Very thin pads
Pads that are clean and dry

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads that are clean and dry
questions.explanation: When checking brakes, look for cracked drums, pads covered in oil or grease, and worn or broken pads. Clean, dry pads are good.

questions.question: On a shipping paper with both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, how should the hazardous materials be marked?

options.text: Highlighted in a bright color.
Circled with a pen or marker.
Written the same way as non-hazardous materials.
Written in red ink only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Highlighted in a bright color.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials can be identified by highlighting them in a contrasting color.

questions.question: What should you do when you start the engine during the pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Listen for strange noises.
Rev the engine.
Turn up the radio.
Turn on the heater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen for strange noises.
questions.explanation: When you start the engine, listen carefully for any unusual sounds.

questions.question: Why should cargo tanks never be completely full?

options.text: Liquids expand as they heat up.
Regulations require space between the liquid and the tank roof.
The tank would be too heavy.

questions.correctAnswerText: Liquids expand as they heat up.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in the tank because liquids expand when heated. Different liquids expand different amounts.

questions.question: What must you do to complete a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest?

options.text: Sign it by hand.
Sign it only if you cross into another state.
Sign it only if weather conditions were bad.
Have a witness sign it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sign it by hand.
questions.explanation: You must sign the manifest by hand. Include the name and EPA number of all shippers, carriers, and the destination on the manifest.

questions.question: When transporting chlorine and approaching a railroad crossing, what must you do?

options.text: You must stop before crossing the tracks.
You must slow down before crossing the tracks.
You can cross without stopping if no warning lights are flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop before crossing the tracks.
questions.explanation: When transporting chlorine, always stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track at every railroad crossing, even if no train is coming.

questions.question: When checking your tires before a trip, what should you look at?

options.text: Tire pressure.
Tire color.
Tire manufacturer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tire pressure.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check that tire pressure is correct. It should not be too low or too high.

questions.question: How do you check for a leak in hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times and hold it for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down as far as possible and let go. If the pedal does not return to normal, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down as far as possible and let go. If the brake squeaks, there may be a problem.
Remove the rear wheel and listen for noise when you press the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times and hold it for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
questions.explanation: To check hydraulic brakes, pump the brake pedal three times. Then press it firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak or another brake problem.

questions.question: Why is proper coupling technique important?

options.text: It is the same on all vehicles.
It is essential for safe vehicle operation.
It requires that the fifth wheel plate is not greased.
It can be learned over time.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is essential for safe vehicle operation.
questions.explanation: Proper coupling and uncoupling technique is critical for safe operation of combination vehicles. Improper coupling can be very dangerous.

questions.question: Why is backing with a trailer dangerous?

options.text: It is hard to see what is behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot move in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to see what is behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing a truck is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Avoid backing whenever possible.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, where should you not park?

options.text: Within 300 feet of a bridge.
Within 40 feet of the road.
For only short periods of time.
On grass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within 300 feet of a bridge.
questions.explanation: Do not park a vehicle carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. Only park briefly for necessary vehicle operations like refueling.

questions.question: How can you avoid a hazard?

options.text: Always steer to the left.
You may be able to drive onto the shoulder.
Steer sharply in one direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be able to drive onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: In an emergency, driving onto the shoulder may help you avoid a hazard. Most shoulders are strong enough to support a large vehicle.

questions.question: How do ice cream trucks create hazards for other drivers?

options.text: Ice cream trucks must be kept cold.
Children often run toward ice cream trucks without looking for traffic.
Ice cream trucks leave water and ice on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Children often run toward ice cream trucks without looking for traffic.
questions.explanation: Ice cream trucks are hazardous because they attract children. Children often do not see or pay attention to other vehicles when running to or from ice cream trucks.

questions.question: What is required for hazardous materials shipments?

options.text: Shipping papers are not needed for most shipments.
Shipping papers are required for all shipments.
Shipping papers can be kept in a digital file only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shipping papers are required for all shipments.
questions.explanation: Shippers of hazardous materials must provide shipping papers. These papers tell drivers about the dangers of the materials.

questions.question: When checking tires, which of these is not a problem?

options.text: Too much air pressure
Too little air pressure
Mixing radial and bias-ply tires
Rear tires with at least 2/32 inch of tread

questions.correctAnswerText: Rear tires with at least 2/32 inch of tread
questions.explanation: Check that air pressure is correct. Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread. Rear tires need at least 2/32 inch of tread. Do not mix radial and bias-ply tires.

questions.question: In an empty combination vehicle, stiff suspension springs and strong brakes will have:

options.text: High traction.
Low traction.
No traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low traction.
questions.explanation: An empty combination vehicle stops more slowly than a loaded one. With less weight, the stiff suspension springs and strong brakes have lower traction.
